-82.70750,28.01040.name: Florida Fertility Institute
-82.70750,28.01040.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Mark D. Sanchez, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-46.65356,-23.55966.name: Lab For Life Centro de Medicina Reprodutiva
-46.65356,-23.55966.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://labforlife.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-80.24820,43.54480.name: Semex Alliance
-80.24820,43.54480.desc: A Canadian cattle genetics organisation owned by its member breeders rather than by shareholders, and one of the small group that dominates bovine artificial insemination worldwide alongside the listed and cooperative firms in Europe and North America. It owns its own reproductive technology company, which is the pattern worth recording across this facet: the same firms now control both the sorting technology and the genetic catalogues, so a farmer buying semen is buying from an organisation that owns both halves and can no longer be played against a rival on either.

-56.09790,-15.60140.name: Associação Mato-grossense dos Produtores de Algodão (AMPA)
-56.09790,-15.60140.desc: The cotton producers' association of Mato Grosso, Brazil's largest cotton state, which created and funds the research institute that breeds the varieties its members grow and tests the chemicals they buy. A trade association that owns its own research capacity is unusual on this map: most of the associations recorded here lobby and publish, while the testing is done by contractors or by the state. Where growers fund the trials, the studies answer to the people planting the crop rather than to the company selling the trait — which is a genuinely different arrangement, whatever one concludes about the results.

116.27500,39.99500.name: Chinese Academy of Forestry — State Key Laboratory of Tree Genetics and Breeding
116.27500,39.99500.desc: Where the world's first commercialised engineered tree came from. Work began in the late 1980s, a Bt gene was put into black poplar in 1989, field testing followed in 1994, and the State Forestry Administration approved two clones for commercial planting in 2002 and 2003 — the first anywhere. Roughly 1.4 million trees went into 300 to 500 hectares; a 2016 count put the area at 543 hectares. The target was the beetle damage running through China's 7 million hectares of clonal poplar. The programme was assisted between 1990 and 1995 by an FAO project funded through the UN development programme, and by a long working relationship with a German federal forestry research centre. An engineered forest tree in commercial ground for two decades is the single most informative thing in this facet, and it is not in North America or Europe.
